title: cross-sdk-compat-layer-and-ergonomic-stream-consumer-batching
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Introduces a cross-SDK compatibility shim for streaming auth/reauth and a consumer-friendly stream API across Python/TypeScript/Go. Bumps SDK versions: py 2.3.0, ts 1.13.0, go v1.9.0. Adds batching-friendly retry presets and Windows signal handling for graceful shutdowns.
description: Context: Multiple teams requested consistent streaming ergonomics and auth/reauth behavior across the three official SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). This PR implements a lightweight compatibility layer in the monorepo to centralize retry profiles, stream consumer semantics, and signal/shutdown handling so SDKs can converge without duplicating policy logic. Motivation: parity gaps were causing subtle production regressions (different backoff curves, resume semantics, and platform shutdown behavior). Goals: 1) provide a single source of truth for retry/backoff presets used by all SDKs, 2) standardize streaming consumer APIs (async iterator in Python, async generator / AsyncIterable in TS, context-aware streamer in Go) and 3) add platform-specific shutdown handling (improved Windows Ctrl-C/signal handling) and a small set of batching presets for low-latency / high-throughput workloads. Summary of work: - New compat module: sdk/compat/retry_presets.go / retry_presets.py / retryPresets.ts which define named retry bundles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and serialization hooks so SDKs can embed them at build time. - Streaming API harmonization: Python: introduced StreamClient.iter_lines() typed async iterator and StreamConsumer helper for backpressure hooks; TypeScript: added AsyncGenerator-based consumer helpers plus small adapter for Node/Browser differences; Go: added StreamCursor interface that accepts context.Context for clean cancellation and a StreamAdapter that mirrors TS/Py semantics. - Auth & reauth: centralized token refresh policy and heartbeat hint protocol so SDKs can exchange short lease tokens and run the same refresh jitter logic. - Batching presets: server + client hints to encourage smaller/larger batch windows depending on latency budget; clients surface an ergonomic batchingHint option. - Windows and signal handling: previously the Go SDK's interrupt logic was Linux-first; added a small cross-platform signal shim and e2e test to validate graceful KV cache flush on Ctrl-C on Windows runners. - Docs and examples: updated docs/sdk/streaming.md with cross-language examples and migration notes, added examples/streaming/prefix_cache.py and examples/ts/streaming_demo.ts. - Tests: unit tests in each SDK package for parity cases, integration smoke tests in ci/workflows/sdk-integration.yml. Checklist: - [x] compat/retry_presets implemented and exported - [x] Python async iterator facade added and documented - [x] TypeScript async generator helpers added and documented - [x] Go context-aware StreamCursor implemented - [x] Token refresh policy centralized and validated - [x] BatchingHint option surfaced in client constructors - [x] Windows signal shim + e2e test added - [x] CI matrix updated to run py/ts/go streaming suites - [x] Version bumps for all three SDKs Local testing: ran unit tests across SDKs and the integration smoke suite locally and on CI windows-latest, ubuntu-latest, macos-latest. Observability: added short-lived telemetry hooks so the platform can measure retry counts and reauth latencies (opt-in by default to protect privacy). Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature gate; SDKs will publish subsequent releases once the compatibility package lands in the build artifacts. Breaking changes: none by default; new ergonomic APIs are additive and migration notes are in the docs. Related: references ENG-2345 (streaming parity), ENG-4512 (token lease refactor), SUP-987 (customer-reported reconnects).

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can we avoid importing the entire compat package into the runtime hot path? Suggest lazy load + serializing presets into a small JSON blob included in builds.
Evelyn Park: Good point; switched to serialized presets embedded at build time in build/release/manifest.json to keep runtime footprint minimal.
Priya Natarajan: In Python, the async iterator surface looks good but please add an example for handling backpressure when consumers are slow.
Evelyn Park: Added consumer_helpers.py with documented usage and included example in docs and examples/streaming/prefix_cache.py.
Connor O'Reilly: Windows runner e2e is flaky on first run due to timing; recommend adding a small retry or longer timeout to the ctrl-c validation.
Evelyn Park: Increased timeout and added one retry attempt in the windows job; re-ran CI and verified stability.
post_merge_notes: Follow-up: publish SDK packages after release job includes the compat manifest. Plan to cut python 2.3.0, typescript 1.13.0, go v1.9.0 in the next release window. Monitor new telemetry for retry spikes for two weeks; rollback plan is to flip feature gate in the platform and republish SDKs with previous default presets if needed.
